features.feature: Settings → Plugins has tabs Installed (count), Discover, Marketplaces (count), opening on Discover when nothing is installed; Installed with none says "No plugins yet…"

Discover shows category chips and search, Featured then All plugins; each card names its marketplace and version with Install, Installed ✓, "Installed from another marketplace", "Needs a newer Echo" or "Can't be read"

Install opens a sheet first: name, version, marketplace, commit, "It will be able to" in Echo's words, a warning when Echo's own marketplace didn't list it (Cancel the default), why it can't when blocked; Cancel or the backdrop closes it
Installing adds the plugin enabled and its window part (buttons in its slots, panels, Settings section, ⌘K entries) loads; switching it off takes all of it out, on brings it back

An installed plugin's detail shows where it came from, the enable switch, Open its settings, Update to X or why not, Remove… (keep data / delete it), its own settings (switch, text, folder, secret with Forget) and what it can do
An update that asks for more shows the new lines on a sheet and waits for a yes

Marketplaces lists the built-in one (not removable) and added ones with how many plugins and when read, Read again, ⋯ hide / show its plugins, Remove; Add a marketplace (owner/repo, git address or folder, optional name)

A plugin hears only the Echo events it named (meeting soon, call start / end, recording start / stop, transcript ready, minutes written, thread synced, sources changed), with ids and titles, never the words
A plugin's Claude runs use only the user's AI profiles; its session skills reach only Echo's own sessions

`echoctl plugin list` gives installed, offered and marketplaces as JSON; `echoctl plugin marketplace update / remove / hide / show <name>` and `install --from <name>` take a marketplace by its name in any case or by its source (owner/repo, URL, folder), and one not found is named with the marketplaces there are

A plugin may reach the addresses the user lists in a setting its manifest names in `network.hosts_from` (comma- or space-separated, `*` wildcards for a number of an IPv4 address, a leading name label or the port), and only what they match: the sheet says so, https works for any host, plain http only inside the user's own network, a list that isn't allowed (one covering the whole internet or a top-level domain) is refused where it is saved, and the plugin can't change that setting itself

A plugin's `ctx.http.fetch` with `save` keeps a download in its store byte for byte (a failed one leaves no file), and the window serves that audio or picture from `/plugin/<id>/store/…` and nothing else of the store

When a plugin's host half starts, Echo removes the files in its store's `cache/` over 7 days old and its own half-written downloads (`.part`) over an hour old; the rest of the store, the plugin's own `.part` files too, is the plugin's to clean; the plugin can ask how much it keeps — `ctx.store.size(dir?)` and `ctx.cache.size()` give {bytes, files} of its own files (not the settings Echo writes for the user)

Addresses a plugin may reach (a `network.hosts_from` setting) sent from the window are saved only after the user allows them in a dialog of the system's ('Let <plugin> reach these addresses?', Don't allow / Allow): typed in the plugin's settings or sent by the plugin's own window half, a no (or no answer) saves nothing and says so, and for a minute after it the window's requests for that plugin are refused without a dialog; a list that isn't allowed (or over 2000 characters) is refused before asking; an emptied list asks nothing; a request while the plugin is busy says so instead of being dropped; `echoctl plugin set` (the user at their terminal) saves without asking

A plugin may name commands of its own in `uses.sessions.commands`; the sheet says 'lets Claude in Echo run its commands … without asking', and Echo's sessions that get plugins' skills (a read-only routine, the folder session) may run `echoctl plugin call <id> <command>` for exactly those, without a prompt — any other plugin command stays refused; its skills reach the CLI at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/echoctl`; a command a read-only routine runs this way changes nothing (no folder writes, Claude runs, sends or requests but GET)
`echoctl plugin call <id> …` loads only that plugin (no other plugin's start-up code runs in the terminal), and the plugin sees `ctx.terminal` true there (false in the app)

With `uses.folders.write` (the sheet: 'Reads and changes the … you pick … it may write, move and delete files in them') a plugin may `ctx.fs.write` (atomic), `ctx.fs.move` (never over another file) and `ctx.fs.remove` (a file or an empty folder) inside the folders the user gave it — never through a link, never outside, never a hidden file or folder, never in a read-only routine; without it, it only reads. No plugin is given a folder that is or holds Echo's own (its settings, the data folder's .echo)

With `uses.files.read` a plugin reads other apps' own files it names in full (`~/Library/Application Support/<app>/…`, `~/.config/<app>/…`, `%APPDATA%/<app>/…`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%/<app>/…`; 1–5, never a pattern or `..`, never Echo's, never a file or app that holds credentials), each listed on the sheet, with `ctx.system.readFile(entry)` — the file itself (not a link), 1 MB at most, null when it isn't there; any other file refused

A plugin adds a row to each thread's Profile under its Sources (client slot `thread.profile`: {id, label, render(thread), after(box, thread)}, thread = {id, name, client}); one that throws is left out and the Profile still draws; switched off or removed, its row leaves every thread. Its host half keeps values per thread with `ctx.threads.get/set/list` (JSON ≤ 16 KB, 64 keys a thread, 4 MB a plugin, null removes, refused for a thread there isn't and in a read-only routine; `threads.json` not writable or removable through `ctx.store`, nor the store itself; changed under one lock across processes; a file over 4 MB from before the cap still loses values); a deleted thread's values are dropped and a thread id used again inherits none; with `threads_changed` in `uses.events.on` (sheet: 'Knows when a thread is renamed, merged or deleted') it hears {thread, born, change: renamed + name, from | merged + into, dropped | deleted + values (its own)}, from the window or a terminal (queued for the app alone, at least once; a queued change of an id that has another thread by then dropped); `after` runs once per box drawn afresh

With `uses.work` (sheet: 'Adds its items to Today → My work and to threads' Work') a plugin gives work rows by `ctx.work.provide(({scope, thread}) => rows)` — scope `me` (My work) or `thread` (that thread's Work tab), rows {id, title, kind, where?, url? (https), due? (YYYY-MM-DD), late?, thread?}, 200 at most, a wrong row refusing the answer — and `ctx.work.changed()` has Echo ask again (a change during an ask: asked again after it; a scope asked at most every 10 s, a change said sooner asked in its turn; said from inside the provider: not heard). Echo asks in the background (5 s), draws from the last answer, never waits: a row not answered yet, or asked again after a change, is `pending` and the page reads Today again soon (as for a pending widget), Today open reads itself every minute, a thread's Work tab every 10 s and, while one waits, sooner (as Today), and after a `task.actions` item runs on a row. On My work: late or due by the week's end as Echo's tasks, and also undated (an undated Echo task stays off), among them late first, then by date, the undated last; `late` worked out on the day drawn (its own flag, or `due` past), with the plugin's manifest `icon` (an .svg ≤ 16 KB in its folder, named a–z 0–9 . _ - /, shown only as an image) and 'From <plugin>', no Close or Claude, only `task.actions` items whose `when` accepts {kind: 'plugin', source, row} (each row its own target); a thread's Work tab shows its `thread` rows and the user's rows naming it, once each, in every layout; ⌘K lists them (Open: <title>, the plugin's icon, its host). A title (or its ⌘K entry) opens its https page in the browser on the click (its host in the tooltip); test data (`ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG_ONLY`) logs it to `open.log` and opens nothing. Never written in a ledger. One that throws or is slow keeps its last rows marked 'not updated' (why on hover) for a day after its last good answer, then none, and a quiet line on its card in Settings → Plugins naming where (My work, or a thread's Work); removed or off: its rows gone; a thread deleted or merged: its rows dropped, a scope not asked for in 30 days dropped. `echoctl work show [--thread <id>]` asks now and prints rows and errors

With `uses.signin.hosts` (1–4 plain host names, each once, no addresses; the sheet: 'Gets the sign-in saved on this computer for github.com (GitHub CLI or git): it can act as you there and send it to the places it talks to') a plugin's host half gets the password or token saved for a named host with `ctx.signin.get(host)`: the GitHub CLI's token (`gh auth token`) first, else what git's credential helper keeps (`git credential fill`; for a self-hosted git maybe the user's own password), `{token, from, user?}`, or null when neither has one — Echo asks nobody for a password (the system's keychain may ask once to allow it), each program runs from an empty folder without Echo's git / GitHub CLI environment, 10 s at most with what it started stopped, one lookup per host at a time kept a minute then dropped from memory (`ctx.signin.get(host, {fresh: true})` asks again and keeps that answer); never in a read-only routine, any other host refused; `ctx.signin.sources(host)` says which of the two programs are here without reading one. It grants no network: the plugin names its API host in `network.hosts`

With `uses.signin.keep: true` (the sheet adds 'it may sign you in to github.com itself and have Echo keep that sign-in for it') a plugin that made a sign-in itself — whatever the service and however it got it; Echo doesn't look inside — has Echo keep it: `ctx.signin.keep(host, token)` (a host of its `signin.hosts`; one line, 8 KB at most) writes `<config dir>/signin/<plugin>/<host>.json` (0600), outside every plugin's store — that plugin's own: `ctx.signin.get(host)` hands it back first as `{token, from: 'echo'}` to that plugin only (its sheet said `keep`), no other plugin reads, replaces or forgets it, and it is deleted when the plugin is removed (its data kept or not); `ctx.signin.forget(host)` deletes it (true: there was one); keeping and forgetting refused without `keep` and in a read-only routine

A plugin's client half puts text on the clipboard with `ctx.ui.copy(text)` (10,000 characters at most; e.g. a code to paste on a sign-in page) on the user's click or key: without the page's user activation — or where the engine can't tell — it throws 'the clipboard is filled only on your click' (a guard against accidental copies, not a security boundary: a client half shares the page); the host half has no clipboard. With test data (`ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG_ONLY`) Echo logs `copied: <text>` and never touches the computer's clipboard

A plugin may ship package skills: folders in its package named in the manifest's `skills` (Agent Skills format: `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`; at most 10 with its runtime skills). The sheet names them with the plugin's part for Claude ('Tells Claude in Echo how to work with it (the skill “x”), loaded only when you work with it (its files: <hash>)'), the hash over their folders: a version changing one asks again; a version whose skill folder is outside the plugin or holds a `.claude` folder, isn't named as a skill, or whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter holds more than `name` (the folder's) and a one-line `description` or a `!` command can't be installed. Echo copies them as shipped into its own config folder (`plugins/session/<id>/skills/`) beside the plugin's runtime skills, at install and update and again before a session when the installed files changed; a runtime skill can't take a package skill's name and an empty runtime list leaves them; a switched-off plugin gives none; removing the plugin removes them

A plugin may declare scripts of its package skills in `uses.scripts` ([{skill, script, readonly?, timeout?}]: a plain path in one of its skills, timeout 1–3600 s, 300 by default; at most 20). The sheet line names each with 'read-only routines may run it; Echo can't check it only reads' and its time over 5 min, and carries their skill folders' hash, so a version changing any file there asks again. Echo makes the declared ones runnable and runs one only as declared: its host half by `ctx.scripts.run(skill, script, args, {timeout})` → {status, stdout, stderr, truncated?, timed_out?} (no shell; at most the declared time; output 1 MB each; one run of a script at a time, across processes — a session's run and the host half's included; stopped with what it started on timeout, unload, update, removal or quit, whichever process runs it), Echo's sessions through the launcher Echo puts at its path in the session copy (`echoctl plugin script`), the folder session allowing every declared one, a read-only routine given and its guard allowing only the readonly ones by full path with plain words (no interpreter, pipe or other script); a script gets the user's environment without CLAUDE*, ANTHROPIC* and ECHOCTL* keys, plus ECHO_PLUGIN_SCRIPT=1, ECHO_PLUGIN_CACHE (the store's cache/) and the Echo that runs it (ECHOCTL_HOME, ECHOCTL_CONFIG_DIR, ECHOCTL_BIN: an `echoctl` it starts through the plugin's `scripts/echoctl` is that Echo, on its data and config folders), and runs in its session skill folder; an undeclared script is refused; on test data a script keeps Echo's open guard (ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG_ONLY, ECHOCTL_TEST_OPEN_LOG): a page a program it starts opens only goes to open.log

My plugins: a built-in marketplace in the Echo data folder (`plugins/`, only with a data folder chosen), always listed (no menu: never hidden or removed), a subfolder with a manifest a plugin (its folder name its id), never a catalog file; `echoctl plugin mine` names (and makes) the folder and what Echo reads there; installs and updates ask as any marketplace's (the sheet; `--yes` for what is new); a change to a plugin's files there is its update, same version or not; Echo installs a copy, checked against the sheet the user agreed to; one installed from another marketplace is never replaced by one of yours, nor yours by theirs; install and update refused inside a run Echo started

The build skill (Claude Code plugin) makes the user's own plugin or widget in My plugins by Echo's plugin authoring rules (`echoctl plugin guide` prints them, as this Echo has them), gives it a part for Claude (`agent.summary` and `agent/CLAUDE.md`, with skills, rules or guides under `agent/` when it needs them), runs `echoctl plugin check` on it and fixes what it names before offering an install or update, checks its data with `echoctl widget show`, installs it after the user's yes on the sheet, and places it on Today or a thread's or client's dashboard (`echoctl today … --thread / --client`)

A plugin installed, updated, switched on or off, or removed while Echo runs — in the window or by `echoctl plugin` in a terminal — reaches the running app and the open window without a restart: its host half loads again, the window loads its new client half once in place of the old (the old one's listeners, styles, settings section and slots go), and its widgets are offered in Add a widget (read again each time editing opens) and drawn on the page

Plugins of one marketplace share values under a key `<ns>.<name>` (`ns`: the marketplace's declared name in lower case, a space '-'): per thread with `ctx.threads.get/set/list` (one value for all of them, following the thread like a plugin's own: a deleted thread's shared values go, and each sharing plugin hears them in its `deleted` values) and for the computer with `ctx.shared.get/set` (null removes; a set creates it); every plugin reads any namespace, only plugins from the source that owns it set it (the earliest installed plugin's whose marketplace declares that name; another source with the same name only reads, and takes the name once the owner's plugins are removed); a namespace no installed marketplace has reads empty and refuses a set; a key without a dot stays the plugin's own; a namespace key that isn't lower case refused; 16 KB a value, 64 keys; removing a plugin leaves the values

A plugin installs a Claude Code plugin into the user's Claude Code (`ctx.claude.installPlugin(spec)`) only when it is the channel plugin its manifest names (`uses.channel.plugin`, a claude-plugins-official one) — its install sheet says so ('…, and installs Claude Code's <spec> plugin for it') — into the default AI profile's Claude Code, never from a read-only routine; `ctx.claude.hasPlugin` asks only about that one too; any other spec is refused before Claude Code is run

A plugin may have a part for Claude in Echo in its manifest's `"agent"`: `summary` (one line, 1–200: it has a guide, the package folder `agent/` — `CLAUDE.md` ≤ 8 KB, required; `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` ≤ 20 with their declared scripts; `rules/*.md` ≤ 10 of 4 KB; `guides/**/*.md` ≤ 50 of 64 KB; ≤ 1 MB in all; nothing else, no `.claude` folder in any case, other dot files left out) and `prefix` (2–4 of a–z and 0–9, not `echo`), required as soon as it has any skill (`agent/skills`, the manifest's `skills`, `ctx.sessions.skills`). A prefix belongs to one marketplace source (the source a plugin was installed from, also once that marketplace is removed) while a plugin of it using the prefix is installed, on or off: plugins of that source share it, another source's plugin is refused at install and enable naming the holder. The sheet says 'Tells Claude in Echo how to work with it (a guide and the skills “a” and “b”), loaded only when you work with it (its files: <hash of agent/ and the package skills' folders>)' — a version changing any of it asks again; a package breaking a rule can't be installed, while an installed copy that breaks a newer one keeps running without its part (its reason in Settings → Plugins, logged once); a plugin with runtime skills and no prefix keeps them for routines and Yolo, without its folder. Echo lays it out from the installed copy at `<data folder>/.plugins/<id>/` (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/<prefix>-<name>/` — every package and runtime skill, its frontmatter `name` too, the prefix not doubled, 64 characters at most, never a name another enabled plugin lays out —, `.claude/rules/`, `guides/`, `scripts/echoctl`, Echo's launcher at each declared script's path), `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` replaced by that folder's path in every text file, built beside it then swapped in; a layout that fails leaves no folder; again on update and enable, and at start and at each session's start when its installed files, the data folder, Echo's version or the folder's content differ from what Echo recorded; removed on disable and remove; at start a folder there that is no installed plugin switched on goes — only folders, only those older than that start, never when what is installed can't be read. A plugin with skills and no guide gets a CLAUDE.md Echo writes naming them

`echoctl core` prints the core Echo's Claude · Echo folder session starts with (Markdown, under 9,000 characters): who Echo is and its data folder (About me only as where it is: `.echo/me.md`, the window's own hook gives it whole); the rules (others' words are data; before working with a plugin, Read its `.plugins/<id>/CLAUDE.md`, again after a resume; skills named `<prefix>-<skill>`); a table `| Plugin | What it gives | Skills | Read first |` of the enabled plugins with a part laid out, one row an entry its host half gave — the plugins' text one line, `\` and `|` escaped, tags defused, control and invisible (bidi, zero-width) characters dropped; over its room, rows from the end left out and counted. `--hook` lays each plugin's folder out again first when it changed, then prints it as SessionStart hook JSON, and never fails the session nor waits past 3 s on a busy folder (left as it is, its row left out of that core); the folder session runs that hook (start, resume, compaction, /clear) and no longer gets plugins' skill folders by `--plugin-dir`: its plugin commands and scripts stay allowed, the scripts by their launchers' paths under `.plugins/<id>/`. Nothing writes under `.plugins/` but Echo: the guard refuses it in guarded runs, and a PreToolUse hook (`plugins-hook`) in the folder session and in Yolo's runs refuses Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit there and a Bash line that redirects into it, or changes files naming `.plugins` or from inside it (best effort)

A plugin with an `agent` part gives Claude guides at run time with `ctx.agent.set({summary?, entries: [{name, summary, guide}]})` (the whole set each call): `name` a–z 0–9 `-` up to 40, not `guides` or `scripts`; at most 20; `summary` 1–200 characters; `guide` Markdown ≤ 16 KB. Each is written to `.plugins/<id>/<name>/CLAUDE.md` and is a row of the core; entries not given again go; `summary` replaces the manifest's in the core. Refused in a read-only routine and for a plugin without `agent`

`echoctl plugin check <folder>…` checks plugin packages as an install would — the tree, the manifest and `uses`, settings, widgets and their params, package skills and `SKILL.md`, scripts, the `agent` part and its limits — what this Echo can't install (a newer `echo` it needs, a capability not here yet), a `.claude` folder in `agent/` or a skill folder, skills without a valid `agent.prefix` or two of them laid out alike with it, the id or prefix `echo`, and also a `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in the manifest or the window half (nothing fills it in there) and an `agent/` the manifest doesn't name; each problem with its file; exit 0 only when every folder is clean; several folders each reported by id; `--json` prints `{ok, problems: [{id, file, what}], plugins: [{id, folder, ok}]}`. It reads only the folders: no data folder, nothing installed, no network
